crowns.lobed: a broadleaf crown: a low dome swelling in five lobes and eight smaller ones
crowns.cone: a conifer seen from above: a steep point, bright on the sunward side, its skirts in shadow, star-edged with eight branches
crowns.umbrella: a flat-topped crown, broad and thin, crisp-edged, standing high on a bare trunk, so its shadow lies far from it: an acacia
crowns.palm: fronds radiating from a point: eight deep lobes
crowns.column: a column with almost no crown: a cactus or a quiver tree, all shadow
crowns.tussock: a clump of grass: a tiny, tight mound, many together
crowns.cushion: a cushion plant or dwarf shrub: a low, dense, rounded mat
crowns.rosette: a giant rosette on a stem: a star of thirteen leaves, as frailejones and giant lobelias
crowns.reed: reeds and papyrus in water: fine, dense, leaning with the wind
crowns.mangrove: a low, dense crown standing in water on its roots

grounds.litter: the forest floor: leaf litter over dark soil
grounds.grass: a sward of grass, fine strokes leaning with the wind, in waves when it blows
grounds.sand: sand in dunes: ridges across the wind, gentle on the windward side, a sharp slip face in lee
grounds.pavement: desert pavement: a scatter of pebbles over pale ground
grounds.salt: a salt flat: white, cracked into polygons
grounds.polygons: patterned ground of the permafrost: ice-wedge polygons
grounds.moss: moss and lichen: soft mats, pale green and grey
grounds.ice: ice: crevasses, and sastrugi carved by the wind
grounds.water: open water between the plants: channels, pools, flood

kinds.ants: colonial foragers in columns between nest and food
kinds.mould: slime mould or fungal network pouring from bright spots
kinds.frogs: small hoppers that sit, hop and call in turn (frogs, lizards, mudskippers, crabs)
kinds.snakes: a banded body winding along (snakes, slugs, and crocodilians in water)
kinds.fireflies: lights that flash and fall into flashing as one
kinds.morphos: butterflies: an erratic, bobbing, flashing flight
kinds.wind: gusts crossing the crowns, turning leaves pale
kinds.blooms: flowers opening florets by the golden angle
kinds.hummers: hoverers that dart between flowers (hummingbirds, sunbirds, honeyeaters)
kinds.troops: a group crossing the crowns in single file, leaping gaps (monkeys, squirrels, lemurs)
kinds.macaws: pairs crossing high and fast between the tallest trees (parrots, hornbills, cockatoos)
kinds.eagles: a raptor circling high, seen only as its shadow
kinds.flocks: birds wheeling as one (the loose dots of DIRT's data pigment)
kinds.herds: grazers moving together over open ground, grazing, then moving on in long files
kinds.hunters: a predator or pack that shadows a herd and at times runs at it
kinds.colonies: a crowd that stays put and seethes: termite mounds, prairie-dog towns, penguins, seals
kinds.swarms: a dense, jittering cloud: mosquitoes, midges, locusts, bees, quelea
kinds.waders: tall birds standing in shallow water, stepping and stabbing (flamingos, herons, storks)
kinds.vees: migrating geese and cranes in V formations, in their seasons
kinds.soarers: vultures and condors circling on thermals, their shadows below
kinds.schools: fish that turn together and flash as they turn
kinds.whales: a great body surfacing, blowing, and sinking again (whales, rays, turtles)
kinds.floes: floes that drift and part: sea ice, or rafts of sargassum
kinds.dunes: sand blowing off the dune crests
kinds.dust: dust devils wandering over hot, dry ground
kinds.leaffall: leaves turning and falling in autumn
kinds.fire: a creeping line of flame through dry grass, leaving a black scar and trailing smoke
kinds.bioluminescence: the sea sparkling where it is stirred, and in the dark

phenology.deciduous: leaves out in spring, full in summer, turning red and gold as the month's mean falls under 10 C, bare under 5 C
phenology.boreal: the conifers green all year; the birch, aspen and larch among them turning gold in autumn and bare in winter
phenology.wet-dry: green in the wet months, gold and leafless in the dry ones; flowering trees at the end of the dry season
phenology.mediterranean: green through the wet winter, gold through the dry summer
phenology.tundra: under snow most of the year; a short summer flush of green and tiny flowers
phenology.desert: bare, blooming only after the rare wet month
phenology.grassland: dormant and brown in the cold; greening in spring; gold where the summer is dry, green where it is wet

phases.fresh: the first leaves of spring, pale and bright
phases.dry: straw and gold in the dry season
phases.bloom: a desert in flower after rain

phase_rules.deciduous: green from 10 C; fresh between 5 and 10 C while warming; turning between 5 and 10 C while cooling; bare under 5 C
phase_rules.boreal: as deciduous, for the colour of the broadleaves among the conifers
phase_rules.wet-dry: green with 3 mm of rain a day or more; dry under 1 mm; between, green if the next month is wetter, dry if not
phase_rules.mediterranean: green with 1.5 mm of rain a day or more and a mean under 20 C; dry otherwise
phase_rules.desert: bloom when the month's rain is at least 1 mm a day and twice the year's mean; bare otherwise
phase_rules.grassland: bare under 5 C; dry with under 1.5 mm of rain a day; fresh between 5 and 10 C while warming; green otherwise

clear.shape: no cloud; at most a contrail

deep convection.shape: towers 34-89 cells across with bubbling edges, anvils streaming downwind, rain shafts under

trade cumulus.shape: small puffs 5-13 cells across in streets along the wind, their shadows beside them

stratocumulus deck.shape: a closed-cell honeycomb sheet, cells 13-21 cells across, with pockets of open cells

coastal fog.shape: a smooth, low veil lying on the coast and in the valleys

storm track.shape: long curved frontal bands and comma-shaped storms, raining

polar stratus.shape: a near-uniform grey sheet, faintly textured

orographic.shape: caps on the summits, banners from them, and smooth lens-shaped wave clouds downwind

cirrus.shape: thin, fibrous streaks along the upper wind, half transparent

fair cumulus.shape: scattered cotton-ball puffs with crisp shadows

broken.shape: broken patches of cumulus and stratus

look_rules.land: the biome's look for the month's phase, drawn toward the soil's own colour as far as the ground is bare
look_rules.snow: where snow lies, the snow look; glaciers, ice sheets, sea ice and frozen lakes wear ice
look_rules.water: lakes and rivers wear lake; the sea wears its warmth, the tropical shallows (reefs and shelf) their own, and upwelling its green
look_rules.matching: paintings are ranked by the CIE Lab distance of their three colours, dark to light, to the look's; a passage wears one of the five nearest, by its own hash

Indomalayan: flame of the forest in flower

*: leaves falling in the dry season

Neotropic: monarch butterflies in their winter clusters

Australasia: grass fire, followed by fire-hawk kites

*: anchoveta and sardines in bait balls
the deep scattering layer rising at night

rules.where: the plane is the Earth: a quarter-degree atlas cell is 233 cells of the plane, east is east, and the plane repeats the Earth every 360 degrees
rules.edges: where one place gives way to another, its edge wanders by up to 144 cells and is dithered across 13, as two sprayed colours meet
rules.vegetation: each stratum's cover is scaled by the place's canopy height over its biome's typical height, so farmland and cities thin the forest they stand in; grass and shrubs thin with aridity
rules.season: the month's mean temperature and rain set the phenology's phase; the month's snow cover whitens the ground by that share, in drifts
rules.light: the sun's noon elevation for the latitude and month sets how long shadows fall; where the sun does not rise, it is night, and above 60 degrees an aurora moves
rules.relief: the ground is shaded by the atlas's elevation, and roughened into ridges as far as its relief runs
rules.clouds: the month's cloud type sets the shapes, and its cloud amount how much of the sky they cover; their shadows fall on the ground
rules.rain: the month's rain (snowfall where the month's mean is below freezing) sets how hard it falls
rules.view: the view distance sets a veil of the sky's colour over the ground: the shorter the view, the thicker the veil
rules.colour: each place wears the saved paintings nearest its look (see LOOKS); nothing is painted in a colour the collection does not have
rules.sea: at sea the ground is water: its depth zone and warmth choose its look, swell runs with the wind, and marine life replaces the land's
